title: George Washington (1732–1799) — Jumonville Glen, Trenton, the Newburgh Spectacles, Annapolis, and the Two-Term Precedent

teenKit.tldr: George Washington wasn't born a marble statue; he was an ambitious, flawed risk-taker who survived military disasters and pulled off the ultimate psychological hack to invent the voluntary surrender of political power.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding Washington reveals how modern democratic stability relies entirely on powerful leaders choosing to step down rather than clinging to absolute control.
keyTakeaways: Washington accidentally kicked off a global conflict called the Seven Years' War as a hotheaded young surveyor in the Pennsylvania woods.

At Newburgh, facing a starving and mutinous army ready to stage a military coup, Washington disarmed them not with threats, but with a pair of reading glasses and a masterclass in silent vulnerability.
By voluntarily handing his military commission back to Congress at Annapolis, Washington shattered the historical cycle of victorious generals becoming dictators.

quiz.question: How did Washington completely shift the room's energy during the Newburgh crisis?

quiz.question: Why was Washington's resignation speech at Annapolis in 1783 historically earth-shattering?
options: It proved that military leaders make the best monarchs
It was the first time a victorious general voluntarily surrendered absolute power back to civilian rule
It officially dissolved the United States government
It announced Washington's run for lifetime emperor
quiz.explanation: Nearly every victorious general before him used their army to seize the throne, making Washington's voluntary surrender of power a radical blueprint for democracy.
